title: Zhat-3 (behavioral proxy B) fidelity sweep: does behavior repair gain-confound FPR?

corrections_20260828.headline: The FPR column and the top-line conclusion (behavior does not repair gain-confound calibration in the empirically plausible regime) SURVIVED independent verification. Three specifics below did NOT and are corrected here. Original numbers are retained unaltered above per Conservation; this block qualifies them.

C1_power_column_is_misleading_as_printed.defect: The 'power' values in results.power_by_fidelity are NOT interpretable and must not be quoted. FPR was computed with a fixed rule (delta > 0.05) while 'power' used a DIFFERENT rule (delta > 95th percentile of the same-fidelity null distribution). Two different tests are printed as one row. Any threshold yielding that power figure has FPR = 0.05 by construction, not the 1.00 reported alongside it.
C1_power_column_is_misleading_as_printed.decisive_evidence: At target_r=0.0 this receipt's own numbers invert: null_delta_mean 0.5647 EXCEEDS pos_delta_mean 0.5537, yet the row still prints power = 0.10. A verifier-computed null-vs-coupled AUC of 0.390 at that fidelity confirms the inversion.
C1_power_column_is_misleading_as_printed.disposition: power_by_fidelity is WITHDRAWN as an inferential quantity. Only fpr_by_fidelity is load-bearing in this receipt.

C2_transition_point_was_under_resolved.corrected: Verifier's finer grid (achieved-r, two independent proxy constructions) locates the transition at r ~ 0.90-0.92: FPR 1.00 up to r=0.80, 0.92 at r=0.85, 0.64 at r=0.88, 0.32 at r=0.90, 0.00 at r=0.92. This sweep's coarse 0.80 -> 0.95 jump could not resolve it. The load-bearing claim is unaffected: the empirically plausible regime (r ~ 0.4-0.6) is far inside the miscalibrated region either way.

C3_framing_calibration_not_information.correction: This is a CALIBRATION failure, not an information failure. At r=0.6 the verifier measured null-vs-coupled AUC = 1.000: the Delta statistic still perfectly separates coupled from uncoupled DATASETS. What is missing is a valid null reference for a SINGLE dataset, which is all real data provides. State the claim as 'required observable-proxy fidelity is ~r >= 0.90, which available covariates do not approach', NOT as 'the distributed-lag statistic carries no information'.
C3_framing_calibration_not_information.caveat_on_the_caveat: This does not reopen the conclusion: the verifier tested a within-dataset trial-permutation null (the only rule an analyst could actually run without oracle knowledge) and it ALSO gave FPR = 25/25 under the gain confound. It further notes that permutation rule is itself non-exchangeable on timing nulls. No runnable decision rule was found that works.
